title: Fibrewise dense opens and maximal-domain birational extension
statement: Let $X\to S$ be a scheme over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], and $U\subseteq X$ open. Define $\operatorname{IsFiberwiseDenseOpen}(X,U)$ to mean that $U_s$ is dense in the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ for every $s\in S$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $q:T\to S$ and let $t:X_T\to X_T$ be a $T$-morphism. Define $\operatorname{HasFiberwiseBirationalExtension}(q,X,t)$ to mean that there are an open $U\subseteq X$ and an $S$-morphism $f:U\to X$ such that $f_T$ is the restriction of $t$ to $U_T$, $U$ is fibrewise dense, $f$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and the image of $f$ is fibrewise dense. Require also that every open $V\subseteq X$ admitting an $S$-morphism $h:V\to X$ with $h_T=t|_{V_T}$ satisfies $V\subseteq U$. Thus $U$ is the full domain of definition, and $f$ identifies fibrewise dense opens. On smooth models over a discrete valuation ring with generic $T$ and separated target, this is precisely an $S$-birational extension represented by an open immersion on its full domain of definition.
